result.title: Query Feedback and Teaching for Stable and Certifiable Language Generation
result.summary: Language generation in the limit studies whether a learner observing an enumeration of an unknown target language can eventually generate only valid, previously unseen elements. We study stability, introduced by Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Velegkas (2025), which requires the generator's infinite output set to eventually remain unchanged, and introduce the stronger notion of certifiability, which requires the generator to determine from its observations that its current output is valid. Drawing on teaching sets in learning theory, we introduce a hierarchy of teaching dimensions for generation under three increasingly strict success criteria: correctness, stability, and certifiability. These dimensions measure the minimum number of selected examples whose appearance guarantees the corresponding success condition. We also study stability and certifiability in the membership-query model of Charikar and Pabbaraju (2025). We characterize stable and certifiable generation, both with and without query feedback, and establish their relationships with uniform generation and identification in the limit. In particular, we give a finite-witness characterization of stable generation, analogous to Angluin's tell-tale characterization of identification, resolving a gap left open by Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Velegkas (2025). We further compare these generation notions with identification in the limit and contrast their teaching requirements on well-studied language families, including regular and erasing pattern languages.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在「极限语言生成」框架下引入可认证性（certifiability）这一强于稳定性的准则，并用教学维度刻画正确、稳定、可认证三类生成目标所需的最少示例，同时分析带查询反馈的成员查询模型下稳定与可认证生成的特征及其与极限辨识的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从观测即可判定当前输出有效」的可认证性与教学维度，可能为 LVR 中「证据是否充分、何时停止推理并输出」的 STOP 决策与最小监督信号提供形式化视角，但属纯文本学习理论，需核查可迁移性。
